blocks.text: There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, autumn and winter. *Spring* is the season when flowers start to grow and the weather is nicer than in summer. *Summer* is very hot in North America. Many people go to the beach in summer time to get suntanned and feel better than at home, but many of them get sunburned. *Autumn* is called fall too. It is the time when the leaves fall down from the trees and the wind blows everywhere. *Winter* is terrible in the United States. The snow falls day and night and the temperature is very low. It is very cold in winter. All Americans are very happy when the weather reporter says: “winter has just finished”. People should wear warm clothes during the winter in order to keep themselves from catching a cold.

items.q: How many seasons are there in a year?
When do flowers start to grow?
Is summer hot or cold?
Where do many people go in summer?
When do the leaves fall down from the trees?
Does the wind blow in autumn?
Does it snow in winter?
What should people wear in winter?
What season do you like most?
Would you practice any sports in winter?
Do you get wet when it is raining?
Don’t you think it is rather hot today?

blocks.text: The sun *is* a star. It *rises* at 6 o’clock in the morning. My cousin Henry *got up* from bed this morning when the sun *had* just *risen*. Then, *he went* to school at seven, after spending half an hour in the bathroom and half an hour having breakfast. He always *goes* to school on foot, but this morning his neighbor *gave* him a ride. He *has been taking* Henry to school these days because his father sometimes *lends* him the car. Yesterday afternoon, Henry *arrived* late to the “school concert”. He *felt* bad with his neighbor for *he had been playing* the trumpet until midnight, and didn’t ask him for a ride.

items.q: What is the sun?
What time does it rise?
When did Henry get up?
How long did it take him to have breakfast?
How does Henry always go to school?
Who did give him a ride?
Did Henry arrive late to the concert?
